analysis.label: 信号
analysis.text: 诉苦情绪句即落点。这句以 I'm getting a little fed up(我快受够了)这种带强烈不满情绪的 表态领出，正是女方主动开口诉苦的那一句——抱怨题的答案就落在说话人情绪外露、点名 诉苦对象的句子上。

questions.answerText: The ground floor of their cottage was flooded.

analysis.text: The entire ground floor of our cottage was submerged in water and five of us have been living in a caravan ever since. 我们小屋的整个一楼都被水淹没了，从那以后我们五个人一直住在房车里。

analysis.label: 定位
analysis.text: Miss Wilson, according to the notes on your account, the bizarre technical detail that you mentioned refers to the fact that you hadn't paid house insurance the month before the incident. 威尔逊女士，根据您账户上的记录，您提到的那个"古怪的技术细节"指的是，您在事故发生 的前一个月没有缴纳房屋保险费。

analysis.label: 信号
analysis.text: refers to后即解释。男方用 refers to the fact that(指的是…这一事实)这一引子点明缘由， 引子后面那句正是对"bizarre technical detail"的官方解释；据男方说法答原因，就锁定 这句。

analysis.label: 替换
analysis.text: you hadn't paid house insurance the month before the incident ↔ The woman's failure to pay her house insurance in time. 否定句=failure名词化

analysis.label: 排除
analysis.text: A) 未提及 本项盗用前文出现过的 letter 概念制造熟悉感，但男方解释起因时只字未提"女方误读了 信"；misreading the letter 是录音没说的内容，凭空添加。 B) 答非所问 条款 terms and conditions 确在第7段被男方提到 any missed payment in a year will affect the terms and conditions，但男方给"怪细节"的起因是"漏交费"，不是"女方不懂条 款"；本项答非所问。 借用原文：any missed payment in a year will affect the terms and conditions C) 未提及 录音里男方从未说女方"对整件事描述不准"，inaccurate description 是凭空捏造的原因， 与男方给出的"漏交保费"无关。

questions.stem: What does the woman say she would do at the end of the conversation?
questions.stemZh: 这位女士在对话结束时说她会做什么?
questions.answerText: File a lawsuit against the insurance company.

analysis.label: 定位
analysis.text: I've already spoken to him, and you can tell him I'm furious now, and that your company has a lawsuit on its hands. You will be hearing from my lawyer. 我已经和他谈过了，你可以转告他我现在非常愤怒，你们公司要吃官司了。你们会收到我律 师的来函。

analysis.label: 信号
analysis.text: 结尾表态句即落点。对话最后一段女方撂下狠话 your company has a lawsuit on its hands，这是她临挂电话前的行动宣告；题干问 at the end 的打算，落点就在这句结尾 表态。

analysis.label: 替换
analysis.text: your company has a lawsuit on its hands ↔File a lawsuit against the insurance company. 撂狠话=提起诉讼

analysis.label: 排除
analysis.text: B) 与原文相反 本项盗用第7段男方提议的 manager，但女方第8段开口就回"我已经和他谈过了" I've already spoken to him，找经理是已完成的事，不是她结尾要去做的动作；与原文相反。 借用原文：I've already spoken to him C) 偷换概念 本项盗用 lawyer 一词，但女方说的是 You will be hearing from my lawyer(你们会收到我 律师的来函)——这是"派律师发函/要起诉"，不是"就保单去请教律师"；偷换了她说 lawyer 的真实用意。 借用原文：You will be hearing from my lawyer D) 未提及 terms and conditions 由男方在第7段提到 will affect the terms and conditions of the insurance contract，但女方结尾从未说要"修改合同条款"；revise the terms 是录音没说 的内容。 借用原文：will affect the terms and conditions of the insurance contract 1 W: How do you feel about the future of artificial intelligence? Personally, I feel quite optimistic about it. W: 你对人工智能的未来怎么看？我个人还是挺乐观的。 2 M: AI? I'm not so optimistic actually. In fact, it's something we should be concerned about. M: AI？我其实没那么乐观。事实上，这是我们应该担心的事情。 3 W: Well, it will help us humans understand ourselves better. And, when we have a better understanding of ourselves, we can improve the world. W: 嗯，它会帮助我们人类更好地了解自己。而且，当我们对自己有了更好的了解，我们就能改善这个 世界。 4 M: Well, one thing is for sure: Technology is evolving faster than our ability to understand it. And in the future, AI will make jobs kind of pointless. M: 嗯，有一点是肯定的：技术的发展速度超过了我们理解它的能力。而且在未来，AI会让工作变得毫无 意义。 5 W: I think artificial intelligence will actually help create new kinds of jobs, which would require less of our time and allow us to be centered on creative tasks. W: 我认为人工智能实际上会帮助创造新的工作类型，这些工作需要我们更少的时间，让我们能够专注于 创造性任务。 6 M: I doubt that very much. Probably the last job that will remain will be writing AI software. And then eventually, AI will just write its own software. M: 我对此非常怀疑。可能最后剩下的工作就是编写AI软件了。然后最终，AI会自己编写软件。 Questions 5 to 8 are based on the conversation you have just heard. 7 W: At that time, we're going to have a lot of jobs which nobody will want to do, so we'll need artificial intelligence for the robots to take care of the old guys, like us. W: 到那个时候，我们会有很多没人想做的工作，所以我们需要人工智能让机器人来照顾老人，比如 我们。 8 M: I don't know. There's a risk that human civilization could be replaced by a superior type of digital life. AI will be able to completely simulate a person in every way possible. In fact, some people think we are in the simulation, right now. M: 我不知道。人类文明有可能被一种更高级的数字生命取代。AI将能够以各种可能的方式完全模拟一个 人。事实上，有些人认为我们现在就在模拟中。 9 W: That's impossible. Humans can't even make a mosquito. Computers only have chips. People have brains, and that's where the wisdom comes from. W: 那不可能。人类连蚊子都造不出来。计算机只有芯片。人有大脑，智慧就是从那里来的。 10 M: Once it's fully developed, AI will become tired of trying to communicate with humans, as we would be much slower thinkers in comparison. M: 一旦完全开发出来，AI会厌倦试图与人类沟通，因为相比之下我们的思维速度会慢得多。 11 W: I'm not so sure. A computer is a computer, and a computer is just a toy. W: 我不太确定。计算机就是计算机，计算机只是个玩具。 12 M: Computers can easily communicate incredibly fast, so the computer will just get impatient talking to humans. It will be barely getting any information out. M: 计算机可以非常快速地通信，所以计算机在和人类交谈时会变得不耐烦。它几乎得不到任何信息。 13 W: Well, I believe there is a benevolent future with AI. I also think you watch too many science fiction films. W: 嗯，我相信AI有一个美好的未来。我还觉得你科幻电影看太多了。

questions.stem: What do we learn about the speakers from the conversation?
questions.stemZh: 从对话中我们了解到对话者的什么信息?
questions.answerText: They disagree about the future of AI technology.

analysis.label: 定位
analysis.text: W: Personally, I feel quite optimistic about it. M: AI? I'm not so optimistic actually. In fact, it's something we should be concerned about. 女：就我个人而言，我对它（人工智能）相当乐观。男：人工智能？我其实并不那么乐观。 事实上，这是我们应该担忧的事情。

analysis.label: 信号
analysis.text: 两人态度正面对撞。女方说 I feel quite optimistic about it，男方紧接着以转折否定回应 I'm not so optimistic actually，一个 optimistic、一个 not so optimistic，态度词正面对 撞，这种"一方表态、另一方立刻反对"的应答冲突就是判断两人关系的答案信号。

analysis.label: 替换
analysis.text: optimistic ↔disagree 对立态度概括成分歧 the future of artificial intelligence ↔the future of AI technology 同一话题的同义改写

analysis.label: 排除
analysis.text: A) 原词陷阱 对话里 AI 是两人争论的话题，并没有说他们"分别在 AI 的不同领域工作"；选项盗用了反复 出现的 AI technology 来制造"听到 AI 就想选"的错觉，实则把"谈论 AI"偷换成"从事 AI 不 同分支"。 借用原文：the future of artificial intelligence C) 偷换概念 对话只显示两人对 AI 看法不同，从未比较谁"懂得多懂得少"；differ greatly in their knowledge of modern technology 把"观点分歧"偷换成"知识水平差距"，是录音根本没说 的内容。 D) 与原文相反 both worried 中的"both（都）"与原文矛盾：男方确实担忧，但女方全程 optimistic、 there is a benevolent future with AI，并不担忧。选项盗用了男方 we should be concerned about 的担忧情绪，却错误地扣到"两人都"头上。 借用原文：something we should be concerned about

questions.stem: What will new kinds of jobs be like, according to the woman?
questions.stemZh: 根据女士的说法,新型工作将会是什么样的?
questions.answerText: Less time-consuming and focusing on creation.

analysis.label: 定位
analysis.text: W: I think artificial intelligence will actually help create new kinds of jobs, which would require less of our time and allow us to be centered on creative tasks. 女：我认为人工智能实际上会帮助创造新类型的工作，这些工作会占用我们更少的时间，让 我们能够专注于创造性的任务。

analysis.label: 信号
analysis.text: 被问者的直接描述句。题干问"女方说新工作怎样"，答案就落在女方描述新工作的那句 require less of our time and allow us to be centered on creative tasks——这是被问者 对该对象的直接定性，正是细节题要锁定的应答句。

analysis.label: 替换
analysis.text: require less of our time ↔Less time-consuming 省时间的同义改写 centered on creative tasks ↔focusing on creation 专注创造的同义改写

analysis.label: 排除
analysis.text: A) 张冠李戴 Simply writing AI software 盗用的是男方在后文说的 the last job that will remain will be writing AI software，那是男方对"最后剩什么工作"的说法，并非女方对"新工作"的描 述，张冠李戴。 借用原文：the last job that will remain will be writing AI software B) 未提及 Stimulating and motivating（令人振奋、有激励性）在对话中女方从未这样形容过新工 作，她只说省时和专注创造；这是看似积极、实则原文没有的编造内容。 D) 与原文相反 More demanding and requiring special training（更费力、需专门培训）与女方所说 的"省时、专注创造"方向相反；它更像男方那种悲观论调，与被问者女方的乐观描述对不 上。 借用原文：require less of our time

questions.stem: What is the risk the man anticipates?
questions.stemZh: 男士预期的风险是什么?
questions.answerText: Digital life could replace human civilization.

analysis.label: 定位
analysis.text: M: There's a risk that human civilization could be replaced by a superior type of digital life. 男：有一种风险是，人类文明可能被一种更高级的数字生命形式所取代。

analysis.label: 信号
analysis.text: risk预警词直接领出风险。男方原句以 There's a risk that 直接点出风险，预警信号词 risk 一响，紧跟其后的 human civilization could be replaced by a superior type of digital life 就是答案所在——这种"信号词+正文"是细节题最干净的定位点。

analysis.label: 替换
analysis.text: human civilization could be replaced by a superior type of digital life ↔ Digital life could replace human civilization. 被动改主动的同义句

analysis.label: 排除
analysis.text: A) 张冠李戴 There could be jobs nobody wants to do 盗用的是女方在 a lot of jobs which nobody will want to do 说的话，而且题干问的是"男方"预见的风险，这句既非男方所说、也不是他 眼里的风险，张冠李戴。 借用原文：a lot of jobs which nobody will want to do C) 偷换概念 Humans would be tired of communicating with one another 把原文说反了主语：男方 说的是 AI will become tired of trying to communicate with humans（是 AI 厌倦与人交 流），而非"人类彼此厌倦交流"，主体被偷换。 借用原文：AI will become tired of trying to communicate with humans D) 过度推断 Old people would be taken care of solely by unfeeling robots 嫁接的是女方 robots to take care of the old guys 的说法，且女方把它当作正面用途、并无 solely、unfeeling 之 意；这既非男方预见的风险，又添加了原文没有的"仅靠、无情"。 借用原文：the robots to take care of the old guys

options.text: There could be jobs nobody wants to do.
options.textZh: 可能会有没人愿意做的工作。

options.label: B
options.text: Digital life could replace human civilization.
options.textZh: 数字生活可能取代人类文明。

options.label: C

questions.stem: What is the man's concern about AI technology?
questions.stemZh: 男士对人工智能技术的担忧是什么?
questions.answerText: It will be smarter than human beings.

analysis.label: 定位
analysis.text: M: Once it's fully developed, AI will become tired of trying to communicate with humans, as we would be much slower thinkers in comparison. 男：一旦 AI 完全发展起来，它会厌倦与人类交流，因为相比之下我们的思维要慢得多。

analysis.label: 信号
analysis.text: 对比中暗示AI更强。男方 we would be much slower thinkers in comparison 用人机对 比，明说人比 AI 慢得多，再加 Computers can easily communicate incredibly fast，这 条贯穿后半段的"AI 远超人类"主线，正是态度题要抓的核心判断。

analysis.label: 替换
analysis.text: we would be much slower thinkers in comparison ↔It will be smarter than human beings. 人更慢即AI更聪明 Computers can easily communicate incredibly fast ↔smarter than human beings 快得多印证更强

analysis.label: 排除
analysis.text: A) 张冠李戴 Life will become like a science fiction film 盗用的是女方收尾的 you watch too many science fiction films，那是女方调侃男方想太多的话，并非男方对 AI 的忧虑，张冠李戴。 借用原文：you watch too many science fiction films B) 原词陷阱 It will take away humans' jobs altogether 借用了男方 AI will make jobs kind of pointless 的工作话题，但题干问的是男方对 AI 的核心"忧虑"，他后半段反复强调的是 AI 超越人类、而非"彻底抢光工作"；altogether 也属程度加码。 借用原文：AI will make jobs kind of pointless C) 原词陷阱 Chips will be inserted in human brains 盗用了女方 Computers only have chips. People have brains 里的 chips、brains 两词，但女方原意是"电脑只有芯片、人有大脑"以 反驳男方，根本没说"往人脑里插芯片"，既张冠李戴又是凭原词拼凑的无中生有。 借用原文：Computers only have chips. People have brains Section B 1 To achieve financial security, how much you save is always more important than the amount you earn or how shrewdly you invest. questions.stem: What do we learn from one of the most researched laws of social psychology?
questions.stemZh: 我们从社会心理学中研究最多的定律之一中了解到什么?
questions.answerText: The more you experience something, the better you'll appreciate it.

analysis.label: 定位
analysis.text: One of the most researched laws of social psychology is something called the "mere exposure effect", which, in essence, means that the more we're exposed to something, the more we tend to like it. 社会心理学中研究得最多的定律之一，叫作“纯粹接触效应”，它的本质是：我们越是接触某 样东西，就越倾向于喜欢它。

analysis.label: 信号
analysis.text: 定义句 means that 引出本质。原文 the most researched laws of social psychology 与 题干完全对上，紧跟的 in essence, means that（本质上是说）是一个明确的下定义信号， 其后那句就是这条定律的核心内容、即答案所在。

analysis.label: 定位
analysis.text: The government's dietary guidelines could have done a lot to lower that climate cost. Not just because of their position of authority: The guidelines drive billions of dollars of food production through federal programs like school lunches and nutrition assistance for the needy. 政府的饮食指南本可以为降低气候成本做很多。不仅仅因为其权威地位：这些指南通过校园 午餐、贫困营养援助等联邦项目，驱动着数十亿美元的食品生产。 52. Why does the author say the USDA could have contributed a lot to lowering the climate cost through its dietary guidelines? A) It has the capacity and the financial resources to do so. B) Its researchers have already submitted relevant proposals. C) Its agencies in charge of drafting the guidelines have the expertise. D) It can raise students' environmental awareness through its programs.

analysis.label: 选项
analysis.text: A) ✓ 正确 their position of authority ↔the capacity drive billions of dollars of food production through federal programs ↔ the financial resources 预判的「权威+经费」两要素分别由 the capacity 与 the financial resources 接住，It has the capacity and the financial resources to do so. 是定位句两个并列原因的完整 概括。 B) 无中生有 Its researchers have already submitted relevant proposals. 把「已提交相关提案」 硬塞进 USDA 的能力来源，但原文没有任何「提案已提交」的信息，第 5 段虽提及科学 报告，但那是顾问委员会的报告而非「USDA 的研究者已提交提案」。 C) 答非所问 Its agencies in charge of drafting the guidelines have the expertise. 说起草机构有 专业能力，但题干问的是「为何 USDA 本可降低气候成本」，专业能力并非定位句给出 的原因——定位句给出的是权威+经费，专业知识只是研究者已存在的事实，不是这一 句话给出的本可降低气候成本的资源。 D) 以偏概全 It can raise students' environmental awareness through its programs. 把「通过联 邦项目影响食品生产」窄化为「通过校园项目提高学生环保意识」。原文 school lunches 只是例子之一，且其作用是 drive billions of dollars of food production（撬 动食品生产），不是提高学生环保意识。 我们从膳食指南咨询委员会的科学报告中了解到什么? A) 食物从农场到餐桌很容易受到污染。 B) 温室效应是一个仍在争论的问题。 C) 现代农业增加了食物多样性。 D) 农业消耗了我们大部分自然资源。

analysis.text: 题干 What should the USDA do to achieve food security according to David Wallinga? 问 Wallinga 提的具体建议，对应原文 Wallinga 的引语必有直陈，无需推断。

analysis.text: 主干是 What should the USDA do，to achieve food security 为目的状语，according to David Wallinga 限定信息源。should 表「应该做什么」，提示答案是建议性陈述。 55. What should the USDA do to achieve food security according to David Wallinga? A) Give top priority to things like nutrition and food security. B) Endeavor to ensure the sustainable development of agriculture. C) Fulfill its mission by closely cooperating with the industries. D) Study the long-term impact of climate change on food production.

analysis.label: 定位
analysis.text: In previous guidelines, they've always been concerned with things like food security—which is presumably the mission of the USDA. You absolutely need to be worried about climate impacts and future sustainability if you want secure food in the future. 在以往的指南中，他们一直关心食品安全这类问题——而食品安全大概也是 USDA 的使 命。如果你希望未来有安全的食品，就必须切实地关心气候影响与未来的可持续性。

analysis.label: 选项
analysis.text: A) 答非所问 Give top priority to things like nutrition and food security. 把 things like food security 和上文 nutrition 拼凑成「优先级最高」，但 Wallinga 并未说「以食品安全为 最高优先级」，而是说「要想拿到食品安全这一结果，必须做可持续性」——重点是手 段（可持续）而非把「食品安全/营养」当目标排序。 B) ✓ 正确 You absolutely need to be worried about climate impacts and future sustainability ↔ Endeavor to ensure the sustainable development of agriculture. if you want secure food in the future ↔to achieve food security 选项 Endeavor to ensure the sustainable development of agriculture. 把 Wallinga 引语后半句的条件因果（要想 X 必做 Y）翻译为目的+行动（为 X 而做 Y），与预判完 全一致。 C) 与原文相反 Fulfill its mission by closely cooperating with the industries. 主张「通过密切配合产 业来履行使命」，但作者第 7 段已批评 USDA 与农业公司 too close to the industries 是问题所在；Wallinga 的话也未提议进一步靠近产业，恰是反方向。 D) 过度推断 Study the long-term impact of climate change on food production. 把 Wallinga 的「关注气候影响与可持续性」推到「研究气候变化的长期影响」。原文要求是「关注 +采取行动」，并非「研究学术问题」，且 study 这种行动属于学术后撤，未对接 Wallinga 的呼吁。

P1 What is the place of art in a culture of inattention? Recent visitors to the Louvre report that tourists can now spend only a minute in front of the Mona Lisa before being asked to move on. Much of that time, for some of them, is spent taking photographs not even of the painting but of themselves with the painting in the background.

P2 One view is that we have democratised tourism and gallery-going so much that we have made it effectively impossible to appreciate what we've travelled to see. In this oversubscribed society, experience becomes a commodity like any other. There are queues to climb Mt. Jolmo Lungma as well as to see famous paintings. Leisure, thus conceived, is hard labour, and returning to work becomes a well-earned break from the ordeal.

P3 What gets lost in this industrialised haste is the quality of looking. Consider an extreme example, the late philosopher Richard Wollheim. When he visited the Louvre he could spend as much as four hours sitting before a painting. The first hour, he claimed, was necessary for misperceptions to be Questions 46 to 50 are based on the following passage. eliminated. It was only then that the picture would begin to disclose itself. This seems unthinkable today, but it is still possible to organise. Even in the busiest museums there are many rooms and many pictures worth hours of contemplation which the crowds largely ignore. Sometimes the largest crowds are partly the products of bad management; the Mona Lisa is such a hurried experience today partly because the museum is being reorganised. The Uffizi in Florence, another site of cultural pilgrimage, has cut its entry queues down to seven minutes by clever management. And there are some forms of art, those designed to be spectacles as well as objects of contemplation, which can work perfectly well in the face of huge crowds.

P4 Olafur Eliasson's current Tate Modern show, for instance, might seem nothing more than an entertainment, overrun as it is with kids romping(喧闹地玩耍) in fog rooms and spray mist installations. But it's more than that: where Eliasson is at his most entertaining, he is at his most serious too, and his disorienting installations bring home the reality of the destructive effects we are having on the planet— not least what we are doing to the glaciers of Eliasson's beloved Iceland.

P5 Marcel Proust, another lover of the Louvre, wrote: "It is only through art that we can escape from ourselves and know how another person sees the universe, whose landscapes would otherwise have remained as unknown as any on the moon." If any art remains worth seeing, it must lead us to such escapes. But a minute in front of a painting in a hurried crowd won't do that. 46. P1 Every five years, the government tries to tell Americans what to put in their bellies. Eat more vegetables. Dial back the fats. It's all based on the best available science for leading a healthy life. But the best available science also has a lot to say about what those food choices do to the environment, and some researchers are annoyed that new dietary recommendations of the USDA (United States Department of Agriculture) released yesterday seem to utterly ignore that fact.

P2 Broadly, the 2016–2020 dietary recommendations aim for balance: More vegetables, leaner meats and far less sugar.

P3 But Americans consume more calories per capita than almost any other country in the world. So the things Americans eat have a huge impact on climate change. Soil tilling releases carbon dioxide, and delivery vehicles emit exhaust. The government's dietary guidelines could have done a lot to lower that climate cost. Not just because of their position of authority: The guidelines drive billions of dollars of food production through federal programs like school lunches and nutrition assistance for the needy. Questions 51 to 55 are based on the following passage.

P4 On its own, plant and animal agriculture contributes 9 percent of all the country's greenhouse gas emissions. That's not counting the fuel burned in transportation, processing, refrigeration, and other waypoints between farm and belly. Red meats are among the biggest and most notorious emitters, but trucking a salad from California to Minnesota in January also carries a significant burden. And greenhouse gas emissions aren't the whole story. Food production is the largest user of fresh water, largest contributor to the loss of biodiversity, and a major contributor to using up natural resources.

P5 All of these points and more showed up in the Dietary Guidelines Advisory Committee's scientific report, released last February. Miriam Nelson chaired the subcommittee in charge of sustainability for the report, and is disappointed that eating less meat and buying local food aren't in the final product. "Especially if you consider that eating less meat, especially red and processed, has health benefits," she says.

P6 So what happened? The official response is that sustainability falls too far outside the guidelines' official scope, which is to provide "nutritional and dietary information."

P7 Possibly the agencies in charge of drafting the decisions are too close to the industries they are supposed to regulate. On one hand, the USDA is compiling dietary advice. On the other, their clients are US agriculture companies.

P8 The line about keeping the guidelines' scope to nutrition and diet doesn't ring quite right with researchers. David Wallinga, for example, says, "In previous guidelines, they've always been concerned with things like food security—which is presumably the mission of the USDA. You absolutely need to be worried about climate impacts and future sustainability if you want secure food in the future."

writing.directions: For this part, you are allowed 30 minutes to write an essay on why students should be encouraged to develop creativity.You should write at least 150 words but no more than 200 words.
writing.model: In an age driven by innovation, the ability to think in original ways has never been more valuable. Therefore, I firmly believe that students should be actively encouraged to develop their creativity, for it benefits both their growth and society at large. First, creativity makes learning far more engaging. When students are free to imagine and design their own solutions, rather than merely memorizing answers, they become genuinely curious and study with real enthusiasm. Moreover, creativity sharpens the ability to solve problems. A learner who is used to exploring different approaches can adapt flexibly to new challenges, which is exactly what future workplaces demand. For instance, many employers today value an engineer who can propose an original design over one who only follows fixed rules. In conclusion, encouraging creativity is far from a luxury; it is a necessity. By nurturing imagination and original thinking, schools equip students to enrich their own lives and to meet the uncertain demands of tomorrow.
writing.modelZh: 【参考译文】在一个由创新驱动的时代，以原创方式思考的能力从未像今天这样宝贵。因此，我坚定地认为，应当积极鼓励学生发展创造力，因为它既有益于他们自身的成长，也有益于整个社会。首先，创造力让学习变得有趣得多。当学生可以自由地去想象、去设计自己的解决方案，而不是单纯地背诵答案时，他们会真正产生好奇心，并带着热情去学习。此外，创造力还能磨练解决问题的能力。一个习惯于探索不同思路的学习者，能够灵活地应对新挑战，而这恰恰是未来职场所需要的。举例来说，如今许多雇主更看重一个能提出原创设计的工程师，而不是一个只会照章办事的人。总之，鼓励创造力绝非一种奢侈，而是一种必需。通过培育想象力与原创思考，学校才能让学生既丰富自己的人生，又足以应对未来那些不确定的挑战。

三连论证落地。'First, creativity makes learning far more engaging' 是观点句，后接一句 解释；'Moreover, creativity sharpens the ability to solve problems' 引出第二个理由；'For instance, many employers today value an engineer who can propose an original design' 用事例把理由说 实，正是'观点+解释+例证三连'。
收束升华落地。'encouraging creativity is far from a luxury; it is a necessity' 换个说法重 申中心立场；'schools equip students to... meet the uncertain demands of tomorrow' 升华到未来意 义，落实'重申升华'。

sentences.text: 主语青藏铁路 + 系动词 is（主语策略：原句主语） 中文已给明确主语 青藏铁路，直接作英文主语 The Qinghai-Tibet Railway。本句中文实为两个判 断："是…高原铁路"和"是…第一条铁路"，都用系动词 is + 表语结构。主干立为 The Qinghai- Tibet Railway is the highest and longest plateau railway in the world。

sentences.label: 降级
sentences.text: 数据与第二个判断降级成同位/独立分句 主干外有三块信息要安放：① 全长1 956公里 译为同位语 with a total length of 1,956 kilometers 或 with a full length of …，挂在主句后；② 其中有960公里在海拔4 000多米之上 用 of which 960 kilometers lie at an altitude of over 4,000 meters 的非限定定语从句承接"全 长"；③ 是连接西藏和中国其他地区的第一条铁路 因信息分量重，单独成一个并列分句 It is also the first railway，再用现在分词 connecting Tibet with the other regions of China 作后置定语 降级"连接…的"。

sentences.label: 语法
sentences.text: 时态 回指全篇基调，陈述铁路现有属性，全句用一般现在时 is / lie。 最高级冠词 最高最长 译为形容词最高级，前面必须加定冠词：the highest and longest，漏掉 the 是常见硬 伤。 数字与单位 1 956 写成英文千分位 1,956；"4 000多米"译为 over 4,000 meters，"多"用 over/more than 表 达；kilometers、meters 用复数。 介词搭配 "在海拔…之上"固定搭配 at an altitude of over 4,000 meters；"连接A和B"用 connect A with B 或 connect A and B。

sentences.label: 译文
sentences.text: The Qinghai-Tibet Railway is the highest and longest plateau railway in the world, with a total length of 1,956 kilometers, of which 960 kilometers lie at an altitude of over 4,000 meters. It is also the first railway connecting Tibet with the other regions of China. 2. 由于铁路穿越世界上最脆弱的生态系统， 在建设期间和建成后都采取了生态保护措施，以确 保其成为一条"绿色铁路"。

sentences.label: 主干
sentences.text: 措施被采取作主干（主语策略：转被动） 中文 采取了生态保护措施 没有动作发出者（谁采取的？没说），是典型的无主句。把承受者"生态 保护措施"提作主语、动词转被动：ecological protection measures were taken。主干立为 ecological protection measures were taken …。

sentences.label: 降级
sentences.text: 原因句与目的句降级成状语 主干外两块都是状语：① 由于铁路穿越世界上最脆弱的生态系统 是原因，降级成 Since/As 引导的 原因状语从句 Since the railway runs through the most fragile ecosystem in the world；② 以 确保其成为一条"绿色铁路" 是目的，降级成 to ensure that… 不定式目的状语。"在建设期间和建 成后"译为时间状语 both during and after its construction。

sentences.label: 语法
sentences.text: 时态 本句偏离全篇基调：采取了 是建设期已完成的历史动作，用一般过去时 were taken（也可用现在 完成时 have been taken）；但原因状语"铁路穿越生态系统"陈述的是持续事实，仍用现在时 runs through。 语态 无主句"采取了措施"必须用被动 measures were taken，不可写成残句 took measures（没主 语）。 最高级冠词 最脆弱的生态系统 译为 the most fragile ecosystem，最高级前加 the。 单复数 "措施"通常复数 measures；ecosystem 此处指那一个特定系统，用单数加 the。

sentences.label: 译文
sentences.text: Since the railway runs through the most fragile ecosystem in the world, ecological protection measures were taken both during and after its construction to ensure that it would become a "green railway". 3. 青藏铁路大大缩短了中国内地与西藏之间的旅行时间。

sentences.label: 主干
sentences.text: 铁路 + 缩短了 + 旅行时间（主语策略：原句主语） 中文主语 青藏铁路 明确，谓语"缩短"取 shorten/reduce，宾语"旅行时间"取 travel time。主干为 The railway has greatly shortened the travel time。承接上文，主语可用 The railway 避免重复 全称。

sentences.label: 降级
sentences.text: 本就是简单句，仅作后置定语处理 中国内地与西藏之间的 修饰"旅行时间"，用介词短语 between mainland China and Tibet 作后置 定语挂在 travel time 后，无需降级从句。整句结构简单，主干立稳即可。

sentences.label: 语法
sentences.text: 时态 "大大缩短了"强调铁路建成至今造成的影响和结果，用现在完成时 has shortened 最贴切，比一般 过去时更能体现"对现在的影响"。 主谓一致 主语 The railway 是第三人称单数，完成时助动词用 has，不是 have。 副词位置 "大大"译为 greatly/significantly，作状语放在助动词与实义动词之间 has greatly shortened。

sentences.label: 译文
sentences.text: The Qinghai-Tibet Railway has greatly shortened the travel time between mainland China and Tibet. 4. 更重要的是，它极大地促进了西藏的经济发展，改善了当地居民的生活。

sentences.label: 主干
sentences.text: it + 两个并列谓语（主语策略：原句主语） 中文主语 它 指代青藏铁路，直接用 it 承接。本句有两个并列动作"促进了…"和"改善了…"，共用主 语 it，立为两个并列谓语：it has greatly promoted… and improved…。主干为 it has promoted the economic development and improved the lives。

sentences.label: 降级
sentences.text: 句首评注语降级成状语 更重要的是 是作者的评注，降级成句首插入状语 More importantly,（逗号隔开），引出后面的主 干，不要硬译成 It is more important that 的笨重句式。"西藏的经济发展""当地居民的生活"分别 用 of / local 处理成名词修饰，无需从句。

sentences.label: 语法
sentences.text: 时态 与上句呼应，"促进了""改善了"造成的影响延续至今，用现在完成时 has promoted… and improved…，全句两个谓语时态保持一致。 主谓一致 主语 it 第三人称单数，并列谓语共用助动词 has；improved 因与 promoted 并列、共享 has，无 需再加助动词。 单复数 "当地居民"不止一人，用复数 local residents；"生活"在此指他们的生活水准，用复数 lives（life 的复数）较自然。 用词 "促进经济发展"搭配 promote/boost the economic development；"改善生活"搭配 improve the lives of …，动词选对才地道。

sentences.label: 译文
sentences.text: More importantly, it has greatly promoted the economic development of Tibet and improved the lives of local residents. 5. 铁路开通后，愈来愈多的人选择乘火车前往西藏，这样还有机会欣赏沿线的美景。

sentences.label: 主干
sentences.text: 越来越多的人 + 选择 + 乘火车（主语策略：原句主语） 中文主语 愈来愈多的人 明确，译为 more and more people 作主语，谓语"选择"取 choose，宾 语为不定式 to travel to Tibet by train。主干为 more and more people choose to travel to Tibet by train。

sentences.label: 降级
sentences.text: 时间状语前置 + 结果分句降级 铁路开通后 是时间状语，前置译为 After the railway was opened / opened（也可 Since the opening of the railway）；这样还有机会欣赏沿线的美景 是前一动作带来的结果/伴随情况，"这 样"指代前面整件事，降级成 which 引导的非限定定语从句 which also gives them a chance to enjoy the scenery along the way，避免另起一句重复主语。

sentences.label: 语法
sentences.text: 时态 "铁路开通后"是过去先发生的动作，时间状语从句用过去时 was opened；主句"愈来愈多的人选 择"陈述开通以来持续至今的现象，回指全篇基调用一般现在时 choose（或现在完成进行更细，但 现在时已足够稳妥）。 主谓一致 主语 people 是复数，谓语用原形 choose，不是 chooses；从句主语 the railway 单数，被动 was opened。 冠词与介词 特指这条铁路用 the railway；"乘火车"固定搭配 by train（train 前不加冠词）；"沿线"译 along the way / along the route。

sentences.label: 译文
sentences.text: After the railway was opened, more and more people choose to travel to Tibet by train, which also gives them a chance to enjoy the beautiful scenery along the way. 英语六级 2020年12月·第1套 · 全卷构成 Part III Part III Part III Part III
